newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's MobileOne offers lower cellular rates.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's MobileOne offers lower cellular rates.

text.p: Singapore's second mobile phone operator said on Tuesday it expected to attract 120,000 subscribers within six months of its launch and offered them lower prices and better services than its rival.
MobileOne, due to launch its cellular phone and paging services in Singapore on April 1, will break Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel) monopoly.
The company unveiled cellular phone packages that officials said could save its subscribers up to 20 percent compared to SingTel.
"They would range from 10 to 20 percent depending on the usage level. At the very high usage level, the savings can be quite significant," chief operating officer Low Chin Nam told a news conference.
MobileOne also announced new paging services which Low said gave its subscribers comparable rates to SingTel.
The company, which officials said has spent about half its projected investment of Singapore $360 million, hoped it would receive some investment returns in five to seven years.
"We are looking to break even within the three to five years of operations and five to seven years for payback for both the cellular and paging markets," chief executive officer Neil Montefiore said.
MobileOne is a consortium comprising Keppel Corp and Singapore Press Holdings, each holding 35 percent, Britain's Cable & Wireless and Hong Kong Telecommunications, each with 15 percent.
MobileOne said it expected to attract about 120,000 cellular phone subscribers between April and October this year and about 100,000 paging subscribers from the first day of its launch.
Asked if MobileOne feared SingTel might react to its plans, Montefiore said:
"I believe SingTel will act in a responsible manner. But if they do lower their prices, we will look at that."
Montefiore said MobileOne would not enter a price war, but instead would emphasise quality, value and customer services.
The company has had about 15,000 cellular phone users trying out its system over the last two months.
Cellular penetration was expected to reach 30 percent in Singapore by year 2000 from 12 percent now, Montefiore said.
The paging market also has room for growth despite its high penetration of 30 percent in Singapore.
"We believe it will start to top out around 40 percent around the year 2000," Montefiore said.
